name: image-generation-loader
title: Image Generation Loader
description: A transparent layer for pictures: a strip of small coloured squares travels down the frame, tinting the image and revealing it as it passes. It can also spell a short word in blocky pixels.
use: An image is being generated or fetched and the wait should feel like part of the reveal.
avoid: The band loops for as long as it is mounted, so it must be removed when loading actually finishes.
a11y: Both layers are aria-hidden and purely decorative; reduced-motion freezes the band instead of sweeping it. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: respected)
looks: Photo tiles with a horizontal strip of tiny square cells laid across them, in blue-green or pink tones. The cells pulse in two shades, a soft glow fades above and below the strip, and a thin caption row sits under each tile.
behaves: The band moves from above the image to below it on a repeating cycle, squares flickering between the two accent colours while the picture shows through. Setting the effect to wave bends the band, scale-wave swells the cells, and text makes the band draw pixel letters.
customise: Effect variant, the two accent colours, optional pixel text, cell size, band height, speed and overlay opacity are props; the pixel font and easing maths live in the file.
weight: moderate: A requestAnimationFrame canvas redraw of a few hundred cells, paused while off-screen.
demo: Three photos: an alpine ridge, white horses in a field, and a smiling woman in a red top, each captioned with a prompt.
issues: The caption text is very small and faint against the dark caption strip.
The pixel word "Generating" set on the first tile is not legible in any frame.
polishWhy: Lively per-cell animation and a convincing reveal; tiny captions and a faint pixel word cost it.
